title: Your Black Friday Deal Is Fake — $1,400 Proof
hook: Black Friday isn't a sale — stores quietly inflate prices in October, then 'slash' them back. Ninety-two percent of deals are cheaper or the same price other times of year.
angle: Retail price manipulation (pre-Black-Friday inflation + manufactured urgency) is documented and legal. Most shoppers have no idea the 'deal' was manufactured — and the FOMO engineering bleeds $1,400 extra out of their holiday budget every year.
audience: Anyone who shops Black Friday — particularly 25–45 year olds who plan a 'budget' but always spend more
key_numbers: 92% of Black Friday deals are cheaper or the same price at other times of year
Retailers inflate prices 30–45 days before Black Friday
Average shopper plans $200 but actually spends $496
$1,400 — average extra holiday spend triggered by Black Friday psychology
60% of wishlist items will be the same price or cheaper in January
